semantics: Built-in native password XOR decoding is enabled automatically by FILEPASS. Other passwords and RC4/CryptoAPI require separately resolved contracts/algorithms; no invented universal CLI password flag.
Framing/BOFs and all standard exempt records remain untouched; BoundSheet offset stays plaintext. Per-record absolute byte position controls the16-byte array phase.
Encrypted continuations are decoded before consumers collect them, preserving SST segments and Unicode option-byte boundaries.
Successful export is plaintext and does not retain/re-emit FILEPASS. Input bytes remain immutable.
Header bounds, aggregate decoded work and periodic cancellation are enforced; no invalid plaintext or refused conversion is published.
XOR has no data authentication; altered structurally valid payloads can remain undetectable. No cryptographic-strength or full encryption support claim.
Only supplied resource bindings are used; no native fallback, ambient credential lookup or password prompt/service is introduced.
